Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 103, verses 1–3:

(p-224) Surat al-'Asr

There are two opinions concerning it.

The first: it is Meccan. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and the majority.

The second: it is Medinan. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and Muqatil.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿By time﴾ — concerning it there are three opinions.

The first: that it is the age (al-dahr). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Farra', and Ibn Qutaybah. God swore by the age only because in it there is a lesson for the observer, from the passing of the night and the day in a measure that never falls out of order.

The second: that it is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), which is the period between the sun's decline and its setting. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

(p-225) The third: the prayer of 'Asr. This was said by Muqatil.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: this is the answer to the oath.

"Al-insan" here means "al-nas" (people), just as you say: "The dirham has increased in the hands of people," meaning the dirhams. "Al-khusr" and "al-khusran" have the same meaning. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "al-khusr" is the destruction or diminution of the capital. So whoever does not employ himself in what brings him lasting profit is in loss, because he has worked to destroy himself, and these two are the greatest of his capital. ﴿Except for those who have believed﴾, that is, who were truthful to God and His Messenger and acted in obedience; ﴿and advised one another to truth﴾, that is, to monotheism, the Qur'an, and following the Messenger; ﴿and advised one another to patience﴾ in obedience to God and in upholding His law.

Ibrahim said in his interpretation of this surah: indeed, the human being, if he is granted a long life in this world, is in decline and weakness, except for the believers, for the rewards of the deeds they used to do in their youth and health are recorded for them.
